text:
Maria: Quick sync — after the outage yesterday I sketched a short list of PRD+runbook changes we need before we re-enable the new routing policy. Please read and comment.

- Goals: reduce blast radius for model capacity saturation, add deterministic fallback, and add clear launch/rollout gates.
- Proposed PRD additions: per-tenant concurrent request cap, automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when queue length > 50, circuit-breaker that trips on token-failures and sustained latency, and explicit QA + canary gates for rollout.
- Acceptance criteria (draft): p95 generation latency <= 250ms under typical load, token-failure rate < 0.5% over 1h, successful canary at 5% for 24h with no severity pages, and cost delta <= 10% relative to baseline.

Raj: Ack. A couple notes from eng: the per-tenant cap needs an opt-out path for enterprise customers who buy dedicated capacity. Also we should require a KV-cache reset plan as part of rollout (cache invalidation caused a cascade last time).

Emily: From SRE perspective add synthetic checks and a short-circuit throttle in the runtime. We should have a synthetic job that hits long seq lengths and multimodal combos every 10m. Alerting: page if 5m rate of token_failures > 0.01 or p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 5m.

Tom: QA will own the canary playbook and add automated perf/regression tests. We need test harness scenarios for: very long prompts, many short bursts, and conversational contexts with KV cache reuse. Acceptance test pass/fail must be automated before unflag.

Kevin: Security/ops ask — ensure KMS key rotation and audit logging still work with smaller-onnx fallback path. Add a step in runbook to validate encryption headers when switching model variant.

Maria: Revised scope suggestion to keep initial launch conservative: implement per-tenant cap + fallback + alerting + canary gating. Defer the advanced autoscale policy (multi-model routing optimization) to milestone 2. We can ship faster if we limit scope. Thoughts?

Raj: I support limiting scope. Implementation notes: the fallback path will be a simple model alias switch, but we must ensure tokenizer parity. We'll add a compatibility check during canary: compare 50 sample inputs across both variants for format differences.

Emily: Runbook steps proposal (short):
1) Detect: Alert fires (token failures or latency).
2) Mitigate: Enable per-tenant throttles -> reduce concurrency to 50% for affected tenants.
3) Fallback: Toggle model alias to small-quantized variant for impacted region.
4) Scale: If mitigation not effective in 10m, trigger emergency capacity (reserved pool) and notify infra.
5) Post-incident: Collect traces and run the new regression suite.

(Example alert rule)
```yaml
- alert: HighTokenFailureRate
  expr: rate(model_token_failures_total[5m]) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Token failure rate > 1% in 5m"
```

Tom: Adding to runbook — include exact escalation list with pager rotations and who can flip the model alias. Also add a checklist for cache reset: graceful drain -> invalidate KV prefix -> warm cache on a small set of tenants.

Maria: Launch gating language for PRD: must pass canary (5% for 24h), zero Sev0/1 pages, automated regression suite green, and runbook owned with contact list. If any gate fails, rollback and open an RFC for compensating controls.

Raj: For scope negotiation with sales — we allow customers to opt into higher caps via dedicated contract. That keeps safety for self-serve.

Emily: One more ops detail: make synthetic job write its results into the console dashboard so product can track regressions over time. Add an alert for synthetic job failures.

oncall-bot: incident-2026-03-19 closed by Emily at 2026-03-19T15:02:10Z (summary: degraded latency due to cache storm).

Maria: Plan of action: I'll update the PRD and draft a short RFC with owners for each item. Raj — you take fallback implementation. Emily — you own alerting and synthetic checks. Tom — QA/canary tests. Kevin — ops/security checks. I'll aim to have the RFC up by EOD tomorrow. Any objections? :thumbsup:

Raj: +1
Emily: +1
Tom: +1
Kevin: +1
deploy-bot: merged branch fix/runbook-hardening into main (CI passed)

Maria: thanks everyone — will post the RFC link here when ready.
